title: Director of Ops
text:
***\*\*\*\*REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION\*\*\*\* Please copy & paste this link to complete a quick assessment:*** ***https://assessment.aptiveindex.com/s/bc6Bof3CrEdo***

**Director of Operations | Red Shovel Landscape** 
*$65,000 to $95,000 DOE + quarterly performance incentives*

**The job in one sentence:** Take daily operations off the owner's plate, and run them better than he did.

Red Shovel is growing faster than its systems. The owner has been the operating system, and he wants out of the daily work so he can focus on vision and growth. You'll report to him. You won't be managing his to-do list. You'll own the results.

**What you'll own**

* Margin, gross profit and crew labor efficiency by department
* Field execution, quality control and callbacks
* Hiring, training and developing crew leads and department heads
* Customer retention and experience
* The systems and reporting that make all of the above visible and repeatable

**What the work looks like**

* **You'll challenge the owner.** He brings big ideas that aren't fully baked. We need you to push back directly and often, and reshape them until they work. If you'd rather execute what you're handed, this isn't your job.
* **You'll fix underperforming departments.** When a crew misses margin targets, you step in, set the direction, make your case to the department head and hold the line until the numbers move.
* **You'll build, not just maintain.** Expect to create repeatable routines (checklists, walk-throughs, audits), standing meetings and handoff rules, and clean labor and margin data.
* **You'll split your time.** Some of it is with crews and department heads, working problems together and keeping good people. The best work often happens alone with the numbers, designing the next fix. When time gets tight, we protect systems and analysis first.
* **You'll move fast, with care where it counts.** Most calls are made without perfect information. Where a miss would hurt margin or customers, such as pricing, bids and the numbers behind reports, you verify before you commit.

**What a great first year looks like**

* The owner is out of daily operations and trusts you to run them
* Department profitability, margin and crew efficiency are up
* Callbacks are down, customer and employee retention are up
* Accountability is clear, and departments hand off work cleanly
* Growth hasn't caused operational breakdowns

**What a bad fit looks like** 
You react instead of plan, you wait for direction, or you treat symptoms instead of causes. You'd end up as one more person the owner has to manage.

**You're likely a fit if you**

* Have led multiple teams (field and/or office), ideally in landscaping, home services, construction or a similar field
* Have built systems that scaled
* Break complex problems into clear steps and fix them at the root
* Are comfortable disagreeing with the boss, and with the data when it doesn't tell the whole story
* Weigh the numbers against what the people closest to the work are telling you

**How we work** 
Leaders serve first. Initiative matters. Excellence is expected. Systems create freedom. Community and accountability drive performance.

**Compensation**

* $65,000 to $95,000 DOE (we value Director of Ops experience from any industry, not just landscape)
* Quarterly incentives tied to results
* 3 weeks PTO/sick leave
* Room to grow as the company does
